name: Home downloads 4.7 MB of the newest episode's audio before anyone presses play
description: Measured on beta.syntax.fm Home, fresh visitor, Chromium at 1400 wide (scratchpad media_bytes.mjs): the player bar's <audio preload="metadata"> (src/lib/player/Player.svelte, src set by player.initialize with the latest show) asks megaphone for the whole 92 MB mp3 and Chrome takes 4,745 KB (67 seconds buffered) before it stops. The rest of the page transfers about 620 KB. The player is in the (site) layout, so every page pays this, and episodes with a video play the video by default, so the audio often goes unused. Fix direction: do not load audio until the visitor presses play (preload none, or set src on first play) and show the episode's length from the database instead of from the file. Check: media bytes on load are 0, the bar still shows the length, play starts audio, a saved position still restores. Not caused by the hero or texture work; the bar has worked this way since it started holding the latest episode on first paint.
result: On beta (v_3 at aedd7503). Audio from the network now waits for play (preload none); Home makes 0 audio requests on load, was 4,745 KB. Scott also asked for the download to be cached: once someone has listened 30 seconds the player keeps the whole episode in the mp3-cache (the save-offline cache), newest 3 kept, listener-saved ones never cleared, skipped when the browser reports data saving or a phone network (Chromium only can tell). Checked on beta in Chromium: kept copy is 94,048,896 bytes exact; return visit plays the device copy with 0 audio requests, length shows on load, position carries over, jump to 25:00 works; video playback still works. Same flow passes locally in Firefox. Home load event on beta, middle of 5: 419 ms, was 995 ms. Costs: the first listen downloads the episode twice (92 MB copy beside the stream, which took 12 MB in the first 5 seconds); without a device copy the bar shows 0:00 for time and length until play. Not checked: return visit in real Safari (Playwright WebKit cannot read its cache back after a reload, even a 10 MB test entry); first visit passes in WebKit. The save-offline pin button is still commented out of the show page (PodcastPost.svelte), so listeners cannot pin an episode themselves. Also fixed: the player remembered a show by its device copy address, which was dead after a reload and dropped the slug and video.

commit.message: Player: audio loads only on play, and listened episodes are kept on the device

name: Fonts: self-host the MDIO variable font instead of fonts.tolin.ski
description:
## Why
Scott, 2026-11-05: get rid of the fonts.tolin.ski font loading and serve the actual MDIO variable font files directly. We get 403s.

## Data (curl with Origin header, 2026-11-05)
| File | Origin syntax.fm | Origin syntax.robo.online | Origin localhost:5740 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MDIOVariable.woff2 (82,320 B) | 200 | 403 | 200 |
| MDIOVariable.woff | 403 | 403 | 403 |
- The woff fallback is 403 everywhere, including production.
- On robo.online the site font fails completely (falls back to local() or the system font).
- The font is a cross-origin request: an extra DNS + TLS connection before text renders in the site font.

## Today
- src/styles/bass.css:32: @font-face '💪' with the 2 fonts.tolin.ski URLs + local('MD IO Variable Regular').
- No MDIO font files in the repo or on the Mac mini.

## Steps
1. Get the real MDIO variable font files from Scott (woff2; no woff needed, every target browser supports woff2).
2. Put them in the repo (static/fonts/ or src/assets for hashed URLs) and point @font-face at them, same-origin.
3. Add <link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin> for the main file and set font-display.
4. Measure before/after on a production build: font request time, time until text renders in the site font, CLS from the font swap. Record numbers here.
5. Check prod, localhost and syntax.robo.online all load it with no console errors.
result:
Self-hosted src/assets/fonts/MDIO-VF.woff2 (converted from Scott's MDIO-VF.ttf with fonttools; byte-identical to the file fonts.tolin.ski served, sha256 2d24093f…). Fingerprinted under /_app/immutable with a one-year immutable cache; preloaded through a preload_fonts handle (SvelteKit sends it as a Link preload header). Dropped the woff fallback (403 everywhere).
4G, cold cache, 9 runs, median. Font downloaded (ms), before → same-origin → + preload: / 8134→8151→6026, /about 690→669→517, /potluck 595→510→359. Font request start: 255–377 → 73–102 ms. First paint +30–110 ms with preload, LCP unchanged. syntax.robo.online now 200 (was 403).
Left: font-display is the default (text hidden up to 3 s while loading). Home's font still competes with 16 MB of thumbnails (60ulzmoe).

commit.message: Self-host the MD IO variable font and preload it

description:
## Why
Scott, 2026-11-10: three separate flickers as /guest/aiden-bai loads on the local dev site, on most pages.

## Found (frame-by-frame recording of the load, scratch flicker.mjs)
1. Dev only: Vite swaps every imported stylesheet in after load. style.css held the @font-face, so the font was declared again (and the first copy removed), the browser loaded it 3 times per page, and all text went blank for a frame each time.
2. Everyone, beta too: the player bar rendered in the browser only, behind an await. For ~60 ms its section had no class (window controls flashed black in the page's top right), then the bar popped in (13% of the screen), then its title arrived and pushed the controls down.

## Fix
- Player bar is server rendered with the latest episode; saved episode swaps in after.
- @font-face + preload in the page head (SiteFont.svelte), out of style.css.
- Admin's browser remembers it (localStorage is_admin), app.html marks the page before paint, admin.css keeps the menu's room. Admin pages render the menu on the server.
- Logo mask preloaded.

## Done when
Recording on local and beta shows nothing moving after first paint beyond the player's seek bar and the admin links filling their own space.

Largest change after first paint, share of screen: local 24% (admin menu) + 13% (player bar) + 4% text blanking twice -> 0.5%; beta 25% + 13% -> 0.5%. What still appears after scripts run: the player's seek bar and volume (0.47%) and the admin links (0.24%), each in room already kept. Font loads once per page in dev (was 3). Logo mask inlined in the CSS (a preload still landed one frame late on beta). Checked on beta: audio play, reload restores the saved episode (title swaps from the latest episode to the saved one), video play, timestamps. Commits 5da7a05b, 4ad144b6, 24d131ba. name: Transcript + tag engine rebuild (xAI STT, OpenRouter, k-means tags) — ON HOLD
description:
## Status
ON HOLD (Scott, 2026-11-09): "lets put a pin in this for now because things might be changing about how we manage this". Don't start until Scott picks it back up.

## Decided
- Transcription: xAI Grok STT called directly (POST https://api.x.ai/v1/stt, model grok-voice-transcribe-2.0). It takes the MP3 by `url` (up to 500 MB), `diarize=true`, repeatable `keyterm` (max 100; reuse src/server/transcripts/fixes.ts keywords). $0.10/hr batch. Scott chose this over OpenRouter STT, which takes base64 only and times out at 60 s, so it would mean chunking and speakers renumbered per chunk.
- Everything else (AI notes, speaker naming, embeddings, cluster names) goes through OpenRouter, so models can be swapped by name.
- Don't store word-level timestamps. Group xAI's words into utterances (speaker change or pause) and save only transcript_utterances. Prod's transcript_utterance_words table is already empty; write a migration to drop it, and Scott runs it.
- Tags are derived automatically by recursive k-means, not chosen from a supplied list (Scott's notes).

## Proposed design (not yet approved)
Pipeline: a Cloudflare Workflow per new episode, started by the podcast sync:
1. Transcribe with xAI.
2. Name speakers: an LLM reads the opening lines plus the host and guest list. This replaces the wes/scott flagger clips in flagger.ts and works for CJ and guests.
3. Save utterances.
4. Write AI notes via OpenRouter.
5. Embed the transcript in 3-minute windows.
6. Tag each window by its nearest tag cluster.

Tag tree:
- Embed every episode's windows (~20k).
- Recursive k-means: split until a cluster is small or tight.
- An LLM names each cluster from its central windows (e.g. JavaScript > Frameworks > Svelte).
- An episode gets a tag when enough of its windows land in that cluster.
- On re-runs, match new clusters to old ones by shared windows so tag slugs stay stable.
- Runs as a Workflow on demand.
- Replaces the 718 old tags, which have duplicates (webdev / Web Development); redirect old /tags URLs.

Alchemy 2.0 has Cloudflare Workflows, Queues, Vectorize and cron support (node_modules/@alchemy.run/cloudflare/src/Workflows).

## Backfill estimate (~$20)
- 99 episodes (#954+) have no transcript: ~$10 with Grok.
- 146 episodes (#906+) have no AI notes: ~$9.
- Embeddings and cluster names for all episodes: ~$1.
- Keep the 954 existing Deepgram transcripts.

## Facts found 2026-11-09
- Tags stopped at ~#906. Old tags came from AiShowNote topics, copied once by scripts/direct-db-migration.js (migrateTopicsToTags). Nothing turns new topics into tags.
- AI notes stop at #906; transcripts stop at #954.
- transcript_utterances is 80 MB (296k rows) in both prod and local.

## Needs from Scott

## Why

name: Snack Pack: going back to the list looks frozen (~2.8 s)
description:
## Bug
Scott, 2026-11-05: go to /snackpack, open an issue, click back. The URL changes to /snackpack but the screen still shows the issue.

## Cause (reproduced in Playwright, Chromium)
- Not stuck, just slow. The list appears after ~2.8 s, with no loading feedback, so it looks frozen.
- src/routes/(site)/snackpack/+page.svelte runs `await get_newsletter_archive()` at the top level. SvelteKit keeps the old page on screen until that resolves.
- get_newsletter_archive (src/lib/newsletter/newsletter.remote.ts) re-runs on every visit:
  - fetchBroadcastList walks every Kit v4 broadcasts page one after another (50 per page, full email content included) to build the list.
  - It also makes a separate subscriber-count call.
  - Measured: about 2.3 s for the remote call.
- /snackpack/__data.json is also requested 3 times per back navigation. Check why.
- The server load's 30-day cache-control on /snackpack/[issue_id] wasn't the cause (ruled out).

## Fix
1. Cache the broadcast list and subscriber count on the server (e.g. module-level value with a TTL of a few minutes, refreshed in the background). The list changes about once a week.
2. Don't block navigation on it: the list page should show at once on back nav.
3. Site-wide: add a navigation progress indicator ($app/state navigating) so any slow navigation never looks frozen. Coordinate with xdtusmbh (perf).
4. Check: list → issue → Back link and browser Back both show the list in under 300 ms.
result: Root cause was routing, not Snack Pack: the (site) layout's onNavigate view transition awaited navigation.complete, and pages with a top-level await only complete after their data loads, so the screen froze on the old page (URL already changed, loading bar hidden) until Chrome aborted the transition at 4 s. Capped the wait at 300 ms. Verified in Playwright: back link and browser Back no longer freeze, loading bar shows, no transition-timeout error, normal navigations still animate. The slow Kit crawl itself moved to xdtusmbh.

commit.message: Stop page transitions from freezing the screen on slow pages

  - src/routes/webhooks/transcripts/+server.ts (300 s)

description:
## Why

## First measurements (local dev server, 2026-11-04; dev mode, so directional only)
| Page | HTML size | Server time |
|---|---|---|
| / (Home) | 768 KB | 0.65 s |
| /guest/adam-argyle | 1.84 MB | 0.13 s |
| /sickpicks | 1.12 MB, 1,717 links | 0.43 s |
| /snackpack | 627 KB | 3.73 s |
| /guests | 452 KB, 179 images | 0.06 s |
| /shows | 244 KB | 0.16 s |
| /show/1016/… | 164 KB | 0.03 s |

Seen so far:
- Home renders 100 feed items up front; no images use loading="lazy".
- Full-page heights: Home 81,000 px, Sick picks 90,000 px (114,000 px on mobile), Guests 89,000 px on mobile. Long lists render everything at once.
- Snack Pack: get_newsletter_archive (src/lib/newsletter/newsletter.remote.ts) re-runs on every visit. It walks every Kit v4 broadcasts page one after another (50 per page, full email bodies) plus a subscriber-count call: ~2.3–3.7 s. Cache it on the server; the list changes about weekly.
- /snackpack/__data.json is requested 3 times per client navigation back to the list. Find out why.
- Guest pages ship ~1.8 MB of HTML.
- The loading bar (src/lib/page_loading_indicator.svelte) starts in onNavigate, which fires only after load functions finish, so slow server loads show no feedback. Consider driving it from $app/state navigating.

## Steps
1. Measure for real: production build (pnpm build && pnpm preview) plus Lighthouse/Web Vitals on Home, Show, Guests, Guest, Sick picks, Snack Pack, at desktop and mobile. Record LCP, INP, CLS, transfer size, JS size.
2. Find the biggest causes, for example: oversized SSR payloads, unpaginated lists, unoptimized/non-lazy images, uncached remote calls (Kit, YouTube), heavy client JS, N+1 or wide Drizzle queries.
3. Agree targets with Scott, then fix the worst first. One subtask per cause.

## Done when
Agreed Web Vitals targets are met on each listed page in a production build, with before/after numbers recorded here.

name: 9A Bulk status operations
description:
## Goal
Enable multi-select status updates in content list.

## Requirements
- Row selection controls
- Bulk action to set status (DRAFT/PUBLISHED/ARCHIVED)
- Batch remote mutation with clear results

## Acceptance Criteria
- Multiple selected rows can be transitioned in one operation
result: Implemented bulk status operations in admin content list with row selection, status target picker, and batch update via bulk_update_status remote command.
